transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get the pre-overtime huddle started. We need to finalize the weekend plan for 480 pump housings on Assembly Cell 8. We've got the standard Saturday and Sunday shifts, each up to 8 hours with two operators. Before I approve the final roster and production controls, I need to hear from workforce coordination, maintenance, and quality on any constraints. Who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I've got a workforce coordination constraint to share. The current certification matrix shows that Saturday's Cell 8 roster must be Lina, who is setup-certified, and Sam, who is run-certified. Sunday's roster must be Ruth, who is setup-certified, and Omar, who is run-certified. I checked the matrix after the last training audit, but the updated roster has not yet been attached to the weekend work order.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've got a maintenance constraint to report. During my morning walkaround inspection of Cell 8, I found that the conveyor servo requires a 90-minute preventive inspection between the Saturday and Sunday shifts. I recorded the finding in my maintenance notebook, but I haven't entered it in the electronic work order yet. We'll need to account for that 90-minute window between shifts.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've got a quality constraint to report. The customer quality amendment requires 12 first-off units after the weekend setup, plus 100% torque verification on the first 30 units after the maintenance restart, with quality signoff before the remaining units can be released. I received the signed amendment by email, but it hasn't been linked to the order record yet. This means Saturday production starts with a 12-unit first-off qualification, and after Sunday's maintenance restart, the first 30 units need full torque verification and my signoff before we continue with the rest.
transcript.speaker: A4
